title: First band: the Ambrose Power job down the river
summary: Barnes's first real job was a four-piece band with Ambrose, Henry Ford and others, playing all night at a dance down the river.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: What was the first band you played in? The first real band?

I'm reading, reading, reading. The first band I played in. I just remember it was, I believe it was Ambrose Power. Ambrose Power. Yeah. Lawrence took his uncle. I played, I played then with them down at Del Cron.
Was he a valve trombone player or a slide? A valve. Valve at that time. Yeah. So we went on down there playing on there.

Well I didn't have many children to play. Got the booty, Casey Jones. And one or two numbers. I could play. The rest I couldn't play. How did you come to get the job? How did they come to hire you? They hired me because he dis-actualy someone I would make the crime for him. So he can't get on me. And I did want to live. Let's see who was an ugly old man for who. Let's see, who's the ugly old man Ford?
Do you have a hood of him? Mm-hmm. Henry Ford, I know.
Henry Ford. He came in on day. And I had a seat with me, Henry Ford, me, Henry Ford Ambrose, and his son, Barty Ford.
Barty Ford? Barty Ford, yeah. What did Henry play on that job?
Bass. Bass. Ambrose on the Chamborne, the old car.

That's right. What kind of a job was it? That was a job. It was a real job. It was down about eight miles in a gasoline boat in a skiff that they told about. Two skiff. All the brilliant things that we had. The bad, some people pick up passes. And we hit down there until about five or six cars in the evening. Got down on the skiff and saw the clay.
We played until six cars in the morning. And who organized the job? Was it a private thing or was it to make money? It was to make money. You got people on there.

You got everything you wanted. Right there, the Samoes. Man, you hear so much of talking about music. You played from six to six, but it looked like it was playing until six or nine. Seven of them. They treated you so nice down there. And you had fun. You drank everything you want. Was this for those Spanish fellows down there?

It was a big difference in the people down there. Yeah. It was a kind of a dance. Yeah. It was a big difference. Yeah. It was like bamboo Perez. Leander Perez. Leander Perez. Oh, and there's a Nunes here. Yeah, it was. But that was down there. But that was down there, it was teetotard's difference from me. Yeah, they were civilized. So these was down here. I don't think I believe that I was fine with shaking. I believe I was having trouble on it with them. But I don't think they get a bad a-go out there, no.
